definitions.explanation: An active attempt to influence, persuade, or engage someone. Often used for diplomatic, organizational, or interpersonal efforts to bring about change.

examples.japanese: {政府|せいふ}への{働|はたら}きかけを{続|つづ}ける。
examples.english: Continue efforts to lobby the government.

examples.japanese: {住民|じゅうみん}への{働|はたら}きかけが{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: Outreach to the residents is necessary.

examples.japanese: {国際社会|こくさいしゃかい}に{対|たい}する{積極的|せっきょくてき}な{働|はたら}きかけが{求|もと}められている。
examples.english: Proactive engagement with the international community is being called for.

notes:
The noun form of the verb {働|はたら}きかける (to work on, to approach, to appeal to). Frequently appears in news and formal writing, particularly in political and organizational contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{働|はたら}きかけを{行|おこな}う (carry out efforts)
・{働|はたら}きかけを{強|つよ}める (intensify efforts)
・{積極的|せっきょくてき}な{働|はたら}きかけ (proactive engagement)
・〜への{働|はたら}きかけ (efforts directed at ~)
